Now then, enjoy your weekend, everyone!

{\q2}and sustained heavy losses after engaging with our own unmanned \Ncombat units—the Juggernauts—and were forced to withdraw.
{\q2}Our forces suffered minimal losses, \Nwith no human injuries or deaths!
{\q2}Defending the nation with our \Nadvanced and ethical drones
has resulted in zero Republic casualties!
{\q2}The day when the righteousness of our nation smashes \Nthe evil remnants of the wicked Empire is not far off!
All hail the Republic of San Magnolia!
Glory to the five-colored flag!
Morning, Major!
Those pigs sure were crying their heads off yesterday.
{\q2}Well, it was a pretty crazy fight. \NI bet at least fifty of them died.
Not that anyone was on board anyway.
Hey, everybody! The doll-loving princess is glaring at us!
Why the angry look, Major Milizé?
It's just a few busted-up drones!
Listen, you—
Morning.
Morning, Annette.
You're up early. You usually sleep in.
I pulled an all-nighter working last night.
Unlike those morons.
Forget about them!
This isn't the battlefield.
We're inside the Gran Mur,
and the enemy will shut down in two years anyway.
{\q2}If anything, you're the weirdo for taking \Nit so seriously for the Republic's sake.
I just think this country's conscience has—
Yeah, yeah.
I'm not awake enough to listen to one of your speeches.
What's that Processor's problem? He's just a part!
No kidding!
{\q2}We're from the First Sector. Why do we have to put up \Nwith those bitching pigs from the Eighty-Sixth Sector?!
Why do you care so much about the drones, Lena?
They're not drones.
I'll put it this way, then.
Why do you care so much about the Eighty-Six?
Looks like the battlefield calls, princess.
Initiate ID confirmation.
Major Vladilena Milizé,
{\q2}commanding officer for the eastern front's \Nninth ward's third defensive squadron.
Para-RAID, activate.

Synchronization complete.
Handler One to Pleiades:
Pleasure to work with you today.
Pleiades to Handler One:
Synchronization successful.
Be careful. The enemy is entering firing range.
Proceed with caution—
{\q2}As always, such kind formalities \Nfor us subhuman Eighty-Six.
How sweet, Miss Human.
{\q2}You're reassigning me to a different unit, \NBrigadier General Karlstahl?
Yes.
{\q2}The truth is, the previous Handler \Ntransferred out of the unit.
As such, we need to find an immediate replacement.
{\q2}If the unit isn't being withdrawn \Nwhile we find a replacement,
does that mean it's defending an important base?
{\q2}Yes, it's the eastern front's first ward's \Nfirst defensive squadron.
Officially called the Spearhead Squadron.
{\q2}It's comprised of veterans from \Nall across the eastern front.
You could consider them an elite unit.
But...
{\q2}I've just been commissioned as a major, \NI don't have the experience for this.
{\q2}And you're also the youngest person \Never to make it to the post of major.
{\q2}If you try to be too humble, \Nyou'll make unnecessary enemies, Lena.
I'm sorry, Uncle Jérôme.
{\q2}I'm sure Václav would be proud \Nif he could see his daughter, too.
How is Margareta?
She's the same as ever—pestering me to get married.
Sounds like her.
{\q2}To be frank, we can't find anyone \Nelse who'll accept the position.
Aren't they an elite unit?
{\q2}Wouldn't it be an honor for a \NRepublic soldier to command them?
Correct, but there are some strings attached.
The unit leader, Personal Name: Undertaker.
He's got a bit of a reputation.
A reputation?
They call him the Reaper.
He has a tendency to destroy his Handlers.
{\q2}The Processor destroys the Handler? \NNot the other way around?
Correct.
It's not just a ghost story?
{\q2}I don't have time in my schedule to share \Nghost stories with my subordinates.
{\q2}Almost all of the Handlers that have been assigned \Nto Undertaker have either retired or transferred.
Some of them even committed suicide.
I know it's hard to believe,
but they claim to be haunted by the "voices of the dead."
The dead?
You're free to refuse, Lena.
You work too hard, anyway.
{\q2}A Handler merely needs to monitor their unit \Nand let those on the field take control—
I'll do it.
{\q2}I'll do my utmost as the Spearhead \NSquadron's commanding officer.
You only need to do the bare minimum.
{\q2}And you should try to keep your \Ninteractions with them to a minimum.
{\q2}Knowing one's subordinates is part \Nof a commanding officer's duties.
Well, while I'm lecturing you, let me add one more thing.
Stop putting the number of casualties in your reports.
Officially, there are no humans on the battlefield.
So there are no casualties.
But that doesn't mean we can ignore them.
What we're doing is unforgivable.
Lena.
You really are just like Václav.
All right.
{\q2}I appoint you, Vladilena Milizé,
{\q2}as the commanding officer—the Handler—of the \Neastern front's first ward's first defensive squadron.
Have the paperwork done by the time you get there.
Best of luck to you.
I'll do my best until my final mission.
So you accepted it?
{\an8}Sheesh...
You're such a weirdo.
It's an honor to command such an elite unit.
Plus, it's worth doing.
And all that stuff about destroying Handlers is a lie, right?
I bet they were slacking and wanted an easy excuse.
It's true that some of them committed suicide.
{\q2}One of Spearhead's Handlers went crazy \Nand blew his head off with a shotgun.
All right, the checkup's done. No problems, as usual.
Thank you for your cooperation.
But why suicide?
Naturally, we were asked to investigate.
{\q2}They thought that it might be \Na problem with the Para-RAID.
Transfers aren't a big deal, but we can't ignore suicides.
What did you find?
Who knows.
You don't know?
{\q2}The Handler was dead. \NHow were we supposed to investigate it?
{\q2}You're the leader of the development team. \NIs that really okay?
We did our jobs.
{\q2}There was nothing wrong with \Nthe RAID Device. End of story.
{\q2}We told them that if they wanted to know more, \Nthey'd have to bring us Undertaker.
{\q2}But those idiots in Transport said, \N"This flight has no seats open for pigs!"
So, you didn't talk to Undertaker?
We just read their report.
No idea, they said.
{\q2}We told them about the dead Handler, \Nand all they said was, "I see."
Well, they're Eighty-Six.
{\q2}It's within the realm of possibility that \Nusing a Para-RAID could lead to insanity.
{\q2}It puts a lot of extra load on the brain to \Nshare sensory data with another person.
And even now, we're only sharing the sense of hearing.
{\q2}If you tried synchronizing vision as well, \Nyour brain just wouldn't hold up.
{\q2}Put too much load on the brain, \Nand you don't come back.
Using the Para-RAID means accepting those risks.
{\q2}But your father was one of the \Npioneers in this field of research.
All of the core principles were developed by someone else.
In truth, there's a lot I still don't understand.
Lena, you really should join us in R&D.
The military's just an unemployment relief right now.
When the Legion shuts down in two years,
{\q2}"former military personnel" isn't going \Nto mean a thing on your résumé.
Thanks.
But we're at war right now.
Those Processors are crazy!
We don't even know the long-term effects of Para-RAIDs.
{\q2}The Eighty-Six die quickly, \Nso the long term doesn't matter.
But I don't want that for you.
Still, it's cowardly.
Right, right.
You really are weird.
I modified the settings.
Oh, Lena! I made chiffon cake.
Want some?
I'll pass for today.
See you later.
I used real eggs.
And real milk.
It's so good!
How's it feel to actually eat the real thing for once?
It's wonderful!
But part of me wonders if this is how it really tasted.
You forget when you eat only artificial stuff.
I've got cream puffs, too.
{\q2}They don't taste like cheese when \Nthey don't have cheese in them,
{\q2}or look like they're about to \Nspit out black smoke, right?
{\q2}Are you talking about the \Ncream puffs I made last time?
It'll be fine this time!
{\q2}I gave some to a potential marriage partner \Nyesterday, and he cried tears of joy.
Sounds like you got a good match for once.
He must've really loved it.
Of course!
{\q2}I also gave him a card with a lipstick kiss \Nand the words, "To my beloved."
{\q2}I dropped them off at the place \Nwhere he's living with his mistress.
